documents.unit: Compass 2035 / AI at Smith Art of Inquiry
documents.title: AI at Smith: Students
documents.stance_why: The page says "Policies vary by course and professor" and tells students to ask; it sets no ban or permission itself, so the decision is handed to instructors (delegates).
documents.summary: The page gives students five expectations: follow each course policy and ask the professor when unsure, disclose and document AI use, verify output, guard personal data, and keep the struggle of learning. It sets no AI rule of its own.

units.why: Heading "Know your course policy" is the first of five expectations; it tells students to learn their course rule, so it is P78 (follow each course's rules), student, course-start, should.
units.anchor: 1. Know your course policy

units.why: "Policies vary by course and professor" states that the rule is set per course and instructor and the page sets none itself, so P04, informs.
units.anchor: Policies vary by course and professor

units.why: "When in doubt, ask your professor before using AI for a class project" is the ask-first rule, P10, student, during-work, should.
units.anchor: When in doubt, ask your professor before using AI for a class project

units.why: "Ask proactively to discuss course expectations and whether AI tools should be part of that process" asks students to start the conversation even without doubt; nearest type is P10 but it is broader than "when unsure".
units.anchor: Ask proactively to discuss course expectations and whether AI tools should be part of that
units.fit_note: Asks students to raise AI expectations proactively with the instructor, not only when unsure.

units.why: "Cite and disclose AI use like other outside sources" requires acknowledgment of AI use, so P24 (disclose with each submission); the "like other outside sources" analogy is secondary.
units.anchor: Cite and disclose AI use like other outside sources
units.fit_note: Frames AI like any other outside source (P45 analogy).

units.why: "Document prompts and tool contributions" tells students to record which tool and prompt contributed, matching P25 (tool, prompt, output) rather than P26 which needs full transcripts.
units.anchor: Document prompts and tool contributions

units.why: "Demonstrate your own thinking so your professors can respond to you and help you learn" keeps the student as the thinker visible to the instructor, P32 (primary problem-solver).
units.anchor: Demonstrate your own thinking so your professors can respond to you and help you learn

units.why: "Keep a human in the loop and check AI-generated information before sharing" asks students to check AI output, so P31 (verify output), with the human-in-the-loop idea as extra.
units.anchor: Keep a human in the loop and check AI-generated information before sharing
units.fit_note: Also asks that a human stay in the loop.

units.why: "Verify claims and check sources" is a verification duty and the reason given, "AI tools predict language patterns, not facts", is that outputs can be wrong; P31.
units.anchor: Verify claims and check sources
units.policy: Verify claims and check sources, because AI tools predict language patterns, not facts.

units.why: "Misinformation is always possible—treat responses as a starting point" warns that AI output may be wrong and sets how to treat it; P31, informs.
units.anchor: Misinformation is always possible—treat responses as a starting point

units.why: "Protect personal information and sensitive research data" is a data-protection duty, P50.
units.anchor: Protect personal information and sensitive research data

units.why: "Never enter private data in public unsupported AI platforms" is a prohibition on a data use of AI tools; P50 (protect data, prefer vetted tools), must-not.
units.anchor: enter private data in public unsupported AI platforms

units.why: "Google Workspace is college approved—use Google Gemini and Notebook with your Smith ID" points students to the institution-approved tools, P92 (university-wide, not one course).
units.anchor: use Google Gemini and Notebook with your Smith ID to protect your data

units.why: "Seek out friction in the learning process—wrestling with ideas supports real cognitive growth" gives the reason to not outsource effort, P41 (practice builds skill).
units.anchor: Seek out friction in the learning process—wrestling with ideas supports real cognitive growth

units.why: "Cultivate your own unique voice to say the things that only you can say" values the student's own voice; it fits no type exactly (not skill practice, not fairness), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Cultivate your own unique voice
units.uncovered_note: Students should develop and keep their own unique voice, framed as a value rather than a skill or integrity rule.

units.why: "Interns will provide AI training to students" describes an institutional training offer, P70.
units.anchor: Interns will provide AI training to students

units.why: The Jacobson Center is offered "for writing guidance, brainstorming, planning, and support for revising your writing", a pointer to human help, P72.
units.anchor: For writing guidance, brainstorming, planning, and support for revising your writing.

units.why: Libraries: "Work with Subject Librarians to find authoritative and reliable sources" directs students to human help, P72.
units.anchor: Work with Subject Librarians to find authoritative and reliable sources.

units.why: "Reach out to your professors or class dean when feeling uncertain about policies or overwhelmed by coursework" points to human help; P72 chosen over P99 because the action is contacting people, not easing pressure through resources.
units.anchor: Reach out to your professors or class dean when feeling uncertain about policies or overwhelmed

units.why: "Access the AI Literacy Research Guide" for "more information about AI technologies, ethics, research, and criticism" offers an AI-literacy guide, P70.
units.anchor: Find more information about AI technologies, ethics, research, and criticism.

documents.title: AI at Smith: Faculty and Staff
documents.stance_why: The page offers resources and "help inform AI decisions in the classroom" and refers to "course-specific syllabus policies"; it does not itself ban or permit student AI use, so it delegates.
documents.summary: The page is faculty and staff guidance from the AI steering effort: it points to teaching-center resources, approved tools (Gemini, Notebook), a pilot platform, and data-security limits. It leaves classroom AI rules to instructors.

units.why: "the AI Steering Committee and working groups are leading efforts to provide clear, thoughtful guidance" names the body that owns AI guidance, P80.
units.anchor: the AI Steering Committee and working groups are leading efforts

units.why: "how artificial intelligence can enhance learning, spark creativity, and streamline daily work" names benefits without a rule, P87.
units.anchor: how artificial intelligence can enhance learning, spark creativity, and streamline daily work

units.why: "We recognize both the opportunities and the distinct responsibilities... committed to helping members of the Smith community make confident, informed decisions" is a principle-level preamble, P56.
units.anchor: committed to helping members of the Smith community make confident, informed decisions around engaging with

units.why: "We prioritize the protection of data and privacy" states a privacy principle, P50.
units.anchor: We prioritize the protection of data and privacy

units.why: "maintaining the accuracy and integrity of any content created with assistance from AI" asks for accuracy of AI-assisted content, P31.
units.anchor: maintaining the accuracy and integrity of any content created with assistance from AI

units.why: "these tools support, not replace, the original work and critical thinking of the faculty and staff" says AI must not replace thinking, P32, here addressed to faculty and staff.
units.anchor: these tools support, not replace, the original work and critical thinking of the faculty and
units.fit_note: Applies to faculty and staff, not students.

units.why: "a new video resource will be available to use as a tool to facilitate course discussions on the use of generative AI" gives instructors a resource to discuss AI with students, P66.
units.anchor: a new video resource will be available to use as a tool to facilitate course

units.why: The video covers "the importance of understanding course-specific syllabus policies", i.e. students must know each course's rules, P78, informs.
units.anchor: the importance of understanding course-specific syllabus policies

units.why: "emphasizing our students' authentic intellectual development and encouraging their responsible exploration" pairs learning protection with encouragement; no type holds both, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: emphasizing our students’ authentic intellectual development and encouraging their responsible exploration of these technologies
units.uncovered_note: Frames AI guidance as protecting authentic intellectual development while encouraging responsible exploration.

units.why: "a set of tailored documents intended to help inform AI decisions in the classroom" is support for instructors deciding policy, P63.
units.anchor: a set of tailored documents intended to help inform AI decisions in the classroom

units.why: "Departments across the college are identifying potential ways to leverage enterprise-wide AI tools" concerns operational AI use outside teaching, P76.
units.anchor: identifying potential ways to leverage enterprise-wide AI tools

units.why: "Smith College has approved specific AI tools, including Google Gemini and Notebook, for general use by faculty and staff" names the institution-approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: Smith College has approved specific AI tools, including Google Gemini and Notebook

units.why: "Smith ITS provides guidance and resources... step-by-step instructions, practical use-case ideas, and key data privacy information" supports employees learning AI; P63 is faculty-learning support, here covering staff too.
units.anchor: Smith ITS provides guidance and resources for the use of AI tools
units.frag_end: guidance and resources for the use
units.fit_note: Support is for employees (faculty and staff) and includes data privacy information.

units.why: "piloting a platform that enables faculty and students in their courses to experiment with... Claude and OpenAI's GPT models" is a sanctioned course-level AI platform, P17.
units.anchor: piloting a platform that enables faculty and students in their courses to experiment

units.why: "interactive training sessions and workshops held by the ITS department" is AI training for employees, P70.
units.anchor: interactive training sessions and workshops held by the ITS department

units.why: "Submit a request for an AI tool data security review" is the review step before enabling an AI tool, P65.
units.anchor: Submit a request for an AI tool data security review
units.frag_end: Submit a request for an AI

units.why: "Confidential data cannot be used in AI tools unless the CIO/Counsel has made an exception" bans confidential data in AI; P50 chosen over P80 because the main content is the data rule, not who grants exceptions.
units.anchor: Confidential data cannot be used in AI tools unless the CIO/Counsel has made an exception
units.fit_note: Also names the CIO/Counsel as the exception authority (P80).

documents.title: Academic Integrity Board Information for Faculty
documents.stance_why: The Board tells faculty to "state exactly whether and how students are allowed to use this technology in your course" and gives only examples of what a course might restrict; it sets no rule itself, so it delegates.
documents.summary: The Academic Integrity Board's faculty page explains how to report suspected violations, why detectors should not be relied on, and how to state AI expectations. It asks faculty to decide what to allow in each course.

units.why: "Invite the student to talk about the situation. Approach the conversation non-judgmentally" asks faculty to talk with the student before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: Invite the student to talk about the situation.

units.why: "inform the student that you are reporting the situation to the Academic Integrity Board" is a required procedural step, P81.
units.anchor: inform the student that you are reporting the situation to the Academic Integrity Board

units.why: "To report a case to the AIB, please use the Academic Integrity Board Reporting Form" names the required form, P81.
units.anchor: please use the Academic Integrity Board Reporting Form
units.frag_end: please use the Academic Integrity Board

units.why: "Proving that the work ... was actually generated by AI is not a straightforward task" admits AI use is hard to verify, P82.
units.anchor: is not a straightforward task

units.why: "AI-detecting software can be an unreliable indicator of whether content was generated by AI" states detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: AI-detecting software can be an unreliable indicator of whether content was generated by AI

units.why: Detectors "more likely to yield false positives" for non-native English speakers and neurodivergent writers names a bias harm of detectors; P53 over P39 because the point is bias against groups.
units.anchor: work by certain people, like non-native English speakers and those who are neurodivergent, is more
units.fit_note: Concerns bias of AI detectors against particular groups, not AI tools themselves.

units.why: "you should never rely on this software to prove that a student has used generative AI" forbids relying on detectors, P39, must-not.
units.anchor: you should never rely on this software to prove that a student has used generative

units.why: "The AIB does not rely on the results of AI-detecting software to make decisions about cases" states the Board's own practice, P39.
units.anchor: The AIB does not rely on the results of AI-detecting software to make decisions about

units.why: "We strongly encourage faculty members to learn about the limitations of AI-detecting software" asks faculty to educate themselves; P63 (faculty learning AI).
units.anchor: We strongly encourage faculty members to
units.frag_end: learn about the limitations of AI-detecting
units.fit_note: Learning is about limits of detectors rather than AI tools in general.

units.why: "The AIB strongly encourages faculty to submit all cases of suspected violations to the Board" is a reporting procedure, P81.
units.anchor: The AIB strongly encourages faculty to submit all cases of suspected violations to the Board.

units.why: "it is simply unfair to students when some faculty are more likely to report cases than others" grounds reporting in fairness, P95.
units.anchor: it is simply unfair to students when some faculty are more likely to report cases

units.why: "driven not by a punitive mandate, but by an educational mandate" says misconduct is handled educatively, P68.
units.anchor: driven not by a punitive mandate, but by an educational mandate

units.why: "the Board's most common sanction is to lower the grade on the piece of coursework in question" states a typical penalty, P37.
units.anchor: the Board’s most common sanction is to lower the grade on the piece of coursework

units.why: "We also keep records of all cases" (to track repeat violations and trends) describes record-keeping; no type fits, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: We also keep records of all cases.
units.uncovered_note: The Board keeps records of all integrity cases to track repeat violators and trends in violations.

units.why: "make your expectations and course policies clear on your course's syllabus" requires a syllabus statement of expectations, P09.
units.anchor: make your expectations and course policies clear on your course’s syllabus

units.why: "Be sure that you state exactly whether and how students are allowed to use this technology in your course" asks for an explicit generative AI statement, P09.
units.anchor: state exactly whether and how students are allowed to use this technology in your course

units.why: "Reinforce those expectations every time students are working on an assignment" repeats the communication at each assignment; nearest type P09.
units.anchor: Reinforce those expectations every time students are working on an assignment.
units.fit_note: Asks for repeating the expectations at every assignment, not only in the syllabus.

units.why: "students can make erroneous assumptions in cases where no expectations about the use of generative AI are stated on the syllabus" explains why a statement is needed; P09 (rationale), not P06 because no fallback rule is given.
units.anchor: students can make erroneous assumptions in cases where no expectations about the use of generative
units.fit_note: Gives the reason; no default rule for silent syllabi is stated.

units.why: "speak with students about the importance of academic honesty for the learning process" asks faculty to explain the reasons, P66.
units.anchor: speak with students about the importance of academic honesty for the learning process

units.why: "Holding discipline-specific conversations at the beginning of the semester" sets timing for talking about integrity costs, P66.
units.anchor: Holding discipline-specific conversations at the beginning of the semester

units.why: "The Academic Integrity Board has seen an increase in cases regarding the use of generative AI" reports data on misuse, P55.
units.anchor: The Academic Integrity Board has seen an increase in cases regarding the use of generative
units.fit_note: Evidence is about misconduct cases, not learning outcomes.

units.why: "Students are using generative AI as learners in many ways: as a study partner, to generate quiz questions..." recognizes study uses as legitimate; P14 (study aids).
units.anchor: as a study partner, to generate quiz questions, to hear alternative explanations of concepts, to
units.fit_note: Also names explanations of concepts (P12) and summarizing readings.

units.why: "learn about the ways that students use generative AI and make decisions about what you will allow in a given course" leaves the decision to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: make decisions about what you will allow in a given course

units.why: "if your course focuses on building students' critical reading skills, you might state that students are not allowed to use generative AI to summarize course readings" ties the rule to learning objectives, P83.
units.anchor: if your course focuses on building students’ critical reading skills, you might state that students

units.why: "speak with students about the importance of developing one's own voice as a writer" asks faculty to discuss the reasons, P66.
units.anchor: speak with students about the importance of developing one’s own voice as a writer

units.why: "Using generative AI to write a paper removes an opportunity to develop that voice" says AI writing shortcuts skill-building, P41.
units.anchor: Using generative AI to write a paper removes an opportunity to develop that voice.

units.why: "we often can tell students that the papers lacked a clear point of view or a strong voice" describes spotting AI papers by their lack of voice; not an evidence standard (P69) nor a detector rule, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: we often can tell students that the papers lacked a clear point of view or
units.uncovered_note: The Board reports recognizing AI-generated papers by a missing point of view or voice.

units.why: "Talk with your students about what is sacrificed if they use AI to substitute for their own thinking" asks faculty to discuss the reasons, P66.
units.anchor: Talk with your students about what is sacrificed if they use AI to substitute for

units.why: "please consider sharing your assignments with colleagues" encourages faculty to share AI-teaching strategies, P63 (faculty communities).
units.anchor: please consider sharing your assignments with colleagues
units.fit_note: Peer sharing of AI assignments among faculty.

notes: Coder A. The collect note says the students page tells students to assume AI is not allowed unless stated; the saved text does not say this, so no default-prohibit unit was coded. No school, computing or course documents were included.
